_instructions: A worked example, not a product integration: the GASP subscription, customer, invoice, usage_record and credit_event datasets read from the nightly snapshots a company keeps of its Stripe Data Pipeline tables (schema.sql, snapshot.sql), and the revenue_event dataset from the table derive_cel fills. See README.md.

mappings.notes: Item grain: a Stripe subscription holds one item per price, each with its own quantity, so the item is the subscription GASP sees. A plan swap on one item is an expansion or a contraction of that item; an item added to a subscription is a new subscription with the same customer.

mappings.transform: {{value}} * quantity / 100.0 * (CASE recurring_interval WHEN 'month' THEN 1.0 WHEN 'year' THEN 1.0 / 12 WHEN 'week' THEN 52.0 / 12 WHEN 'day' THEN 365.0 / 12 END) / recurring_interval_count
mappings.notes: unit_amount is in the smallest currency unit (cents for USD) per interval; MRR is the amount for the item's quantity normalised to a month. A metered price (recurring_usage_type metered) has no unit_amount on the item, so a metered item contributes no MRR here; what its usage bills beyond the included volume comes through the usage_record dataset and the usage derivation.

mappings.transform: CASE {{value}} WHEN 'active' THEN 'active' WHEN 'past_due' THEN 'active' WHEN 'unpaid' THEN 'active' WHEN 'paused' THEN 'paused' WHEN 'canceled' THEN 'cancelled' WHEN 'incomplete_expired' THEN 'expired' ELSE NULL END
mappings.notes: past_due and unpaid stay active: Stripe keeps billing and the revenue at risk shows on the invoices. trialing and incomplete have no GASP subscription status (the subscription is not yet billing), so they contribute no MRR; a trial converts into a `new` event on the day it becomes active.
Derived by the nightly job from the customer's subscriptions; Stripe has no customer status.

mappings.transform: CASE {{value}} WHEN 'paid' THEN 'paid' WHEN 'open' THEN 'unpaid' WHEN 'uncollectible' THEN 'written_off' ELSE NULL END
mappings.notes: A paid invoice with amount_remaining > 0 is partial in GASP terms; Stripe reports it as paid once amount_paid covers amount_due, so partial does not occur. void invoices have no GASP status.

Subscription grain: an invoice names the Stripe subscription, not its items, so the invoice derivation's events carry sub_* ids where the item ledger's carry si_*. A company deriving from invoices has no item ledger to clash with.

The period the invoice's licensed lines pay for, written by the nightly job from the line items; null on an invoice with no licensed line (a usage-only or one-off invoice), which the derivation skips.
The licensed lines' amount, prorations and metered lines left out, so MRR is the licensed charge over the months the period covers.
The metered item, so the usage events sit beside the item ledger's with the same grain.
The MRR of the subscription's licensed items on the period's last day, as the nightly job computes it: the commitment Stripe has no field for.

The commitment plus the metered line's charge, which Stripe bills for the calls beyond the volume the licensed price includes. A metered price with no included volume realises every call as usage; a company on such a price records its usage as the metered charge alone and its commitment as 0, outside GASP's scope.

Credit grants belong to a customer, not a subscription, so subscription_id stays unmapped; the balance and consumption metrics do not read it. A grant scoped to prices (applicability_config) is still the customer's balance.

mappings.transform: CASE WHEN {{value}} = 'credit' AND credit_type = 'credits_granted' AND grant_category = 'paid' THEN 'purchase' WHEN {{value}} = 'debit' AND debit_type = 'credits_applied' THEN 'consumption' WHEN {{value}} = 'debit' AND debit_type = 'credits_expired' THEN 'expiry' ELSE 'adjustment' END
mappings.notes: A paid grant is a purchase; a promotional grant, a credit back from a voided invoice and a voided grant are adjustments, positive or negative by type. Stripe's own grant categories, paid and promotional, are the split the ledger needs.

mappings.transform: CASE WHEN type = 'debit' THEN -{{value}} ELSE {{value}} END / 100.0
mappings.notes: Stripe states the monetary amount in the smallest currency unit and the direction in type; GASP signs it like mrr_change.
Every application draws a prepaid balance. Metered usage beyond the credits is billed on the invoice and reaches the ledger through derive_cel target credit_event over the usage records, as overage.

mappings.transform: CASE WHEN credit_type = 'credits_granted' THEN CAST({{value}} AS DATE) END
mappings.notes: The grant's expires_at, on the granting transaction only.
NULL as derived; classify.sql fills it from the item history.
